BiblicalUsage: Neriah is the father of Baruch, and his name frames the most trusted work in Jeremiah's life. Jeremiah hands Baruch the evidence of the purchase of the field, and later calls him to write down all the words of the LORD on a roll — the son of Neriah carrying the prophet's words in both cases.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God uses faithful families: the son of Neriah is the hand that keeps Jeremiah's words when the king burns the roll.
